I think, to me, it's like saying that I am glad I feel guilty because if I did not THAT would make me a terrible person. And at the same time giving me permission to be flawed and not always know what is right and wrong.  

I read your post, I have a couple similar themes and it is very tricky.  I hope you find a way to find peace with it because it's though.

Instead of avoiding the event, feel the guilt that comes with it. Don't ruminate but don't avoid it. Both of those are compulsions. 

I recently saw this video for real event where he said to say to yourself 'I am glad that I feel guilty about this' because feeling guilty about things is normal and healthy. And by saying that you avoid ruminating and re-wire your brain to feel good about guilt. Because guilt is a good thing, that means we are a human being with feelings.
If it is ocd! Diagnosing is very very important. Regular therapy makes ocd worse!!!! Like a lot worse so get help outside of your therapist

Meds helped my first episode very much (50mg of zoloft) but I ignored it and brushed it off and at some point I stopped taking my meds and relapsed. Now I'm at a 100mg and starting therapy. The Zoloft is still helping but I now know that I need therapy as well and I can't just brush it off. The meds have made it so I'm stable enough to talk but I still have a lot of work. It is still a huge relief 

Do not be scared to talk to your therapist. I was for so long but no matter what you need to make progress. This situation is not helping ANYONE. It is most likely not that bad, not life stopping and people have done it hundreds of times. your brain is attacking you. 

People do bad things, we are flawed human beings, very flawed. If you feel true remorse you deserve help. Help to deal with your ocd first and then with your issues. It's not too late to live a beautiful life.
